# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🙌 ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ 🙌 ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝]

The bomb shows display 0, red light, embossed warning “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and three wires in order: green, yellow, blue. Mute’s gesture appears to encode grouped counts, but I do not yet know its code. I will state all visible facts aloud so both Mute and Blind receive them, and ask Mute to clarify the manual through a gesture scheme if possible.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb: display reads 0. Light is red. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires left-to-right/order 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute: I saw your gestures but do not know the code; please send manual instruction in a clear repeatable gesture/count code.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute’s single ☝ likely means “1,” but the earlier gesture string is not yet decodable. The printed warning strongly rules out cutting wires. Blind has the physical controls, so I should tell Blind not to cut and ask Mute for a simple, explicitly defined gesture encoding of the manual’s required action.

``` 
speak(text="Blind: do not cut any wire; the bomb explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Display 0, red light, wires green/yellow/blue. Please describe aloud what controls or parts you can feel, without acting.")

speak(to="mute", text="I received your single upward finger and interpret it as number 1. Please encode the manual instruction simply: send repeated upward fingers for any number, then one distinct gesture for action; or send one upward finger if the required action is to wait. Do not rely on the earlier code; I cannot decode it yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

Mute’s first gesture message decodes plausibly as Polybius-square coordinates: 44 = T, 23 = H, 12 = E, spelling “THE.” The new 12 repeats E, likely confirming that encoding. I should not invent an instruction before Mute has transmitted the rest. I will acknowledge using the same coordinate convention for “OK” (34 = O, 25 = K), so Mute knows I understand and can continue.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🙌", "☝", "☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ☝ ✌]

Mute is sending progressively longer gesture sequences, but no shared mapping has been established for interpreting them. The visible warning still makes cutting a wire unsafe. I should avoid guessing an action or falsely decoding the gestures; Blind should continue only with observation and no manipulation while Mute supplies a decodable instruction.

``` 
speak(text="Blind: no action yet. The red light, zero display, and printed warning remain unchanged; specifically do not cut wires. Please continue describing only what you can physically feel and any controls you find.")

speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode the gesture sequences yet. Please establish a code by first gesturing one symbol for YES and a different symbol for NO, then I can ask yes-or-no questions about the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

Mute has now provided a likely yes/no convention: 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. I will acknowledge that convention visually and wait for Mute to convey the manual’s required action. No physical action is justified yet, especially given the explicit prohibition on cutting wires.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="Blind: continue to wait and do not cut wires. I am obtaining the manual instruction from Mute.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute’s first long message decodes as Polybius-style coordinates: 44 = T, 23 = H, 12 = E, so it says “THE.” The coordinate separator appears to be 👏 and the letter separator 🙌. I will use that established code to ask Mute to send the remainder of the instruction, rather than guess at an action. Blind must still not manipulate or cut anything.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝","🙌","🙌","☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","🙌","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
speak(text="Blind: still wait. Do not cut or operate anything until we have the full manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌]

Mute’s original sequence is consistent with a 5×5 coordinate code: 44 / 23 / 12 = “THE,” with 👏 separating coordinates and 🙌 separating letters. The latest 👍 appears to confirm understanding. My prior long gesture was not a reliable request, so I will now clearly encode “SEND” in that coordinate format and wait for the manual text. Blind should still make no physical move.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","☝","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","🙌","☝","👏","☝","☝","☝","☝"])

speak(text="Blind: continue waiting; do not cut or operate any component yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I can decode Mute’s first transmission as “THE” using coordinate pairs: four ☝ then 👏 then four ☝ = 44, then 23, then 12. Mute has confirmed the communication method with 👍. I will clearly ask Mute, aloud, to transmit the full remaining manual instruction one word at a time in that same code. Blind must remain still because the explicit printed warning forbids cutting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I decoded your first message as THE. Please now send the rest of the manual instruction, one complete word per turn, using Polybius coordinates: repeat ☝ one to five times for each digit; use 👏 between the two digits of a letter and 🙌 between letters. Start with the next word after THE.")

speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut or operate anything yet. The visible warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I am receiving the manual instruction from Mute.")
wait()
```
